name: Vanquisher's Banner
oracle_text:
As this artifact enters, choose a creature type.
Creatures you control of the chosen type get +1/+1.
Whenever you cast a creature spell of the chosen type, draw a card.
blocked_sentences: As this artifact enters, choose a creature type.
Creatures you control of the chosen type get +1/+1.
Whenever you cast a creature spell of the chosen type, draw a card.

needs.what: an 'as this enters, choose a creature type' choice: while the permanent is entering the battlefield (not a triggered ability that resolves afterwards), its controller picks one creature subtype from the whole creature-type list, and the pick is stored on the permanent object for as long as it remains on the battlefield
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The only choice vocabulary is `choose_mode` (DecisionKind.CHOOSE_MODE), which picks among a fixed, card-authored list of effect branches, and `select`-style object choices (CHOOSE_OBJECTS/CHOOSE_PLAYER) that pick objects or players, never a characteristic value. There is no CHOOSE_TYPE decision kind in `engine/enums.py`, and no field on a permanent to record a chosen value; `snapshot` records an object reference so a later effect can read its power/controller, not a free-standing designation. `self_enters` is also a triggered ability that uses the stack, so even a mode-based stand-in would happen after the permanent is already on the battlefield rather than as it enters.

needs.what: a subtype reference that resolves at check time to the type chosen on the ability's own source, usable wherever a literal subtype is written - a static's `affects.subtypes`, a trigger's `filter.subtypes` - e.g. `"subtypes": [{"chosen_type_of": "self"}]`
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `subtypes` in both a selector and a static's `affects` is a plain `list[str]` of literal names validated against the vocabulary at load time (`cards/schema.py`, `AbilityModel.subtypes`), so a static can only ever say a fixed type. `add_subtype` writes a fixed subtype onto affected objects and cannot read one; there is no value expression or binding form that yields a type name rather than a number or an object. Writing `Vampire` (what the existing pool entry does) makes the anthem and the draw trigger apply to a type the player never chose, which is a different card.

needs.what: `spell_cast` needs its `filter` to accept the same chosen-type reference, so 'a creature spell of the chosen type' scopes to the value stored on the trigger's own source rather than to a literal subtype baked into the card file
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The trigger `filter` is an ordinary selector, so it inherits the same literal `subtypes: list[str]` limitation; `binding` reads values the *event* carried (subject, amount, defender), never state stored on the ability's source, so there is nothing for the filter to point at even once the choice can be made and stored.
